evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'By the way, in order for me to give you a quote, I actually need ten to fifteen minutes of your time' but never frames the dependable quote promise or waits for a yes — jumps straight into 'do you have any other concerns aside from the pricing?' No framing, no pause.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked as 'do you have any other concerns aside from the pricing?' — but this comes AFTER the rep has already been probing (property type, floor, elevator access). Timing is late, and it's also narrow (pricing-focused rather than open-ended 'what are your biggest concerns').
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises storage unit pickup, TV mounting/boxing, bed disassembly. Rep asks about TV size, confirms TV wrapping approach, but never says 'tell me more about that' or digs deeper into why these matter. Acknowledges each item once and moves to next logistics question. No real two-layer follow-up.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Rep never reflects back the concerns raised. After customer mentions storage, TVs, and bed disassembly, rep goes straight into technical logistics questions without summarizing 'So what I'm hearing is you're worried about the TV boxes, the storage pickup, and bed takedown — did I get all of it?'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment), floor/stories (3rd floor), rooms (2 bedroom), walking distance (3 min from parking to elevator), additional rooms (none in apartment, storage unit pickup), special considerations (elevator access, white couch, TVs to unmount, beds to disassemble, wood frames), secondary stop (storage unit — climate controlled, 2nd floor with elevator, 5x10, quarter full). Destination (2-story house, 2700 sqft, driveway with garage). All seven logistics items covered.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes — 'normally for a two bedroom we receive 25 to 35 boxes. Do you think you would fall within that range?' Customer confirms yes. Also asked about storage box count.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: No recognizable version of 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' was asked.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives typical range: 'for a two bedroom apartment, we finish the move-in five and a half hours but in your case... estimated hours could be between seven hours to eight hours' and personalizes it to 'elevator and we are doing another pickup at a storage unit and moving everything into two story house... drive time could be between thirty minutes to an hour depending on the traffic.' Anchor is given and personalized.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep discloses hourly rate ($208/hour for two movers), trip fee structure ($12 difference for Friday), 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments: 'minimum of two and a half hours, so after that minimum the time is prorated in. Fifteen minute increments.' Also explains 'not a guess' framing: 'this is only an estimate. If ever the move will take less than this, you will only be charged for how much time we used during the move.' Both elements present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' after giving the estimate. Moves directly to 'we can put you on our schedule' and then into date/time logistics.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar closing. Also, customer asks about bed reassembly near the end ('will they put the bed back together the beds') and rep answers it then, but this is a new concern emerging at the very end of the call, not part of Section 5's loop-closing moment.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asks 'Any more questions before I let you go?' and later 'Any more questions ma'am?' — both are throwaway-style empty questions, not the genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' framing.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No recognizable version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' was asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' Moves straight from pricing discussion into logistics confirmation and booking. No ask for the business.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Date confirmed (October 16th, Friday), arrival window confirmed (8:30 AM to 9:00 AM), both pickup addresses confirmed (2711 West Anderson Lane unit 335, 5715 Burnett Road), destination address confirmed (1531 North Redo Lane), confirmation email to be sent. Phone number (213-716-4512) was captured earlier. Crew size not explicitly confirmed (though 'two movers' was mentioned in rate context). No notes left for crew about customer's concerns (TVs, bed frames, white couch, storage items). Partially complete — missing explicit crew size confirmation and crew notes.

top_strength: Thorough and methodical logistics gathering — the rep captured all seven logistics details with excellent probing on distances, storage dimensions, furniture specifics, and destination layout, laying a solid foundation for an accurate estimate.
coaching_note: Section 1 is missing the quid-pro-quo frame entirely (no 'quote you can depend on' promise or wait for yes), and Sections 5, 6, and 7 are almost entirely blank — no Two Promises (On-Time + Damage Coverage), no final concerns check, no explicit ask for the business, and no rate-lock mention; this needs to be a complete structural rebuild of the back half of the call.
